hooks.A: Why does ice cream make my brain hurt?!

lines.text: Moving day. Boxes everywhere. So I celebrated the only way I know: ice cream, straight from the tub.
Three big spoons later... ow! My head!
Turns out, my brain isn't freezing at all.
When something icy touches the roof of your mouth, the tiny blood vessels there shrink from the cold.
Then, almost right away, they open back up. Fast.
That sudden change sets off nerves behind your nose, and your brain feels it as pain in your forehead.
It even has a fancy name: sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia. Try saying that with a mouth full of ice cream.
lines.say: It even has a fancy name: sfeeno palateen, gangleeo noo ralja. Try saying that with a mouth full of ice cream.

lines.text: Good news: it's harmless, and it usually goes away in under thirty seconds.
Quick fix: press your tongue against the roof of your mouth, or sip something warm.
Or, eat slower. Yeah. Not happening.
Be honest. Am I the only one who didn't know this?
